episode_title: Building a Team and a Brand with Mallory McCaffery of The Bald Kitty Club

real_qa.q: How did Mallory McCaffery transition from working at a corporate waxing franchise to starting The Bald Kitty Club?
real_qa.r: Mallory worked at a corporate franchise for about four years and enjoyed it, but realized she could do it herself and make it more her own. She first started Baja Beauty as a solo operation in a business suite in Toms River, then after becoming busy and needing more visibility and space, she decided to rebrand and open The Bald Kitty Club as a storefront location with multiple waxing rooms.
real_qa.requete: Mallory McCaffery The Bald Kitty Club origin story

real_qa.q: What hiring strategy did Mallory McCaffery use to build her team at The Bald Kitty Club?
real_qa.r: Mallory found that her best team members came to her naturally rather than through active recruitment. Kat reached out via direct message, Sam was referred by someone, and Julia recently contacted her via text. She focused on finding people with the same goals, vibe, and work ethic, and let candidates find her organically, which she says works really well.
real_qa.requete: The Bald Kitty Club hiring team building strategy

real_qa.q: How many waxing professionals work at The Bald Kitty Club and what are Mallory McCaffery's growth plans?
real_qa.r: The Bald Kitty Club currently has four waxing professionals including Mallory, with all four able to work simultaneously in separate rooms. Mallory's goal is to bring on two more team members in the next year and plans to focus on marketing and delegating responsibilities so she can work on growing the business, potentially opening additional locations.
real_qa.requete: The Bald Kitty Club team size expansion plans

real_qa.q: What motivated Mallory McCaffery to leave a safe corporate job and take the risk of opening her own business?
real_qa.r: After watching a podcast episode and hearing about entrepreneurship, Mallory realized she disagreed with certain corporate decisions and believed she could do the job better and make it more her own. She saved aggressively before leaving her corporate job and again before opening The Bald Kitty Club storefront, treating the process like she was in 'squirrel mode' hoarding money to prepare for the transition.
real_qa.requete: why entrepreneurs leave corporate jobs start own business

real_qa.q: Why does Mallory McCaffery still perform waxing services despite owning The Bald Kitty Club?
real_qa.r: Mallory continues to wax clients because she loves her job so much she would do it for free if she could. She values the 20-minute personal connections with long-time clients—some of whom have been with her for eight years—viewing these as refreshing interactions where she catches up on their lives and maintains deep professional relationships.
real_qa.requete: owner still performs service love job clients

guest.bio_context: Mallory McCaffery worked in a corporate waxing franchise for approximately four years before deciding to start her own business. She initially launched Baja Beauty as a solo operation in a business suite in Toms River, New Jersey, then expanded by bringing on her sister Grace part-time during busy seasons, which eventually became a full-time role. After approximately one year, she rebranded and opened The Bald Kitty Club as a storefront location with multiple treatment rooms, growing the team to four waxing professionals including herself.
